start.text: You -- wait. *Wait.* Stand still a moment, friend, I want to be sure.

The priest fumbles a book out of his satchel with hands that shake, and holds it up at arm's length. The pages are warm. He does not seem surprised. He seems like a man who has been waiting a very long time and has run out of ways to say so.
*There.* It is you. Eleven years, and it is *you.*
Forgive me, I have to sit. The knees went years ago and the rest is following.

node.text: A book that would not stop pointing. I followed it out of my own barley field and across a great deal of ground I would not care to walk again. It went warm at night and it pointed, and I went where it pointed, and it pointed *here.*
I will be honest with you: I did not think I would live to see the end of the walk. I cough in the mornings now, and my hands are not good, and I have been eating worse than my own goats.
But I am a priest of the Harvest, and I know what to do with a field that has finally ripened. Sit a moment. Let me say it properly.
He closes his eyes and recites. Not the words you would expect from a farmer -- older than that, and heavier, and he does not stumble over any of it.

The air over his hands begins to curdle. Thin grey light comes off the recitation the way steam comes off a kettle, gathers between his palms, and folds itself flat, and keeps folding, until it is a book.
He opens his eyes and holds it out. He is smiling, and he is tired, and the smile is not entirely for you.
*There.* As many as you need. It was never the paper that mattered.

start.text: The current stops moving the way a current moves. It gathers, and holds a shape it was not holding a moment ago, and the shape is roughly the shape of a person standing very still.
A sound comes off it. Not speech, exactly -- closer to the ringing a struck wire leaves behind, as if the wire had learned one word and were proud of it.

node.text: &W*...hhh...*&y It tries again. The second attempt is worse than the first, which it does not appear to notice.
The face it has assembled is doing the thing a face does when it is trying to remember how far down a chin is supposed to go.
